definitions: A family of waxy lipid molecules composed of sphingosine and a fatty acid. Ceramides are found in high concentrations within the cell membrane of eukaryotic cells, since they are a primary component of sphingomyelin, one of the major lipids in the lipid bilayer.
examples: Ceramides are crucial for skin barrier function.
Many skincare products contain ceramides to help moisturize.
The study investigated the role of ceramides in cell signaling.
